LESSON: TIME, DISTANCE AND SPEED

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: MEASUREMENTS
Topic 3.4: Time, Distance and Speed
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Time, Distance and Speed, part of MEASUREMENTS in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How do we observe speed in daily activities?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Time, Distance and Speed together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: The learner describes the procedure to be followed when measuring distances and time, for example running

track events to determine speed

● Critical thinking and problem solving: The learner studies the instructions before working out and relate time of different

places on the earth

Values:
● Integrity: The learner enhances discipline as they correctly record individual running time during track events and other

games.

● Respect: The learner enhances etiquette as they adhere to their lanes on track events and other games.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

● Safety and security: The learner observes safety measures and time during games and sports.

● Education for Sustainable Development (ESD): The learner participates and chooses careers in games and sporting

activities.

● Self-awareness: The learner participates and times themselves in games.

Link to other subjects:

33

Integrated Science: A learner uses digital devices to tell time in different zones of the world.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Maps in appropriate font and colour contrast, Models of a globe, Digital devices with assistive technology such as screen

readers, screen magnifiers and adapted keyboard, digital watches, meter rule, tactile meter rule, tape measure, print and tactile

maps and Print and Braille Course Book.
